claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: If G-S is cyclic, a shortest residual cycle is chordless and hence induced in G. It is even, and an induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices, so its length is 4, 6, or 8. This proves the equivalence. For an FVS S, each residual component is a tree; diameter at least seven edges would give an induced P8, so its diameter is at most six and its radius at most three. If S is an inclusion-minimal FVS, restoring x creates a cycle containing x; its two neighbors of x are joined inside one component of G-S. Exhaustive checking also passed on all 64,960 P8-free labeled 4-by-4 bipartite graphs and all 16,629,760 deletion sets.
claims.witness: A shortest residual cycle, a diametral tree path, and the cycle created by restoring each vertex of a minimal FVS provide the respective proof certificates.
claims.search_method: Direct graph-theoretic proof, supplemented by exhaustive integer-bit-mask checking of all labeled 4-by-4 bipartite graphs.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: By claim 0, FVS is precisely transversal of the hypergraph whose edges are induced C4, C6, and C8 vertex sets. It has O(n^8) edges and rank at most eight. Branching on every vertex of an uncovered edge has depth at most k and O(8^k) nodes, with O(n^8) scanning work per node. For approximation, the union U of a maximal vertex-disjoint family of hyperedges hits every hyperedge. If the family has p members, OPT is at least p while |U| is at most 8p. The exhaustive checker independently confirmed the equivalence and greedy bound on every P8-free labeled 4-by-4 bipartite graph.
claims.witness: The rank-eight short-cycle hypergraph and any maximal pairwise vertex-disjoint edge family are certificates for the branching and approximation arguments.
claims.search_method: Deductive hypergraph analysis plus exhaustive exact small-graph validation.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: Independent exhaustive generation reproduced the admissible ordered-graph counts at orders 1 through 15 exactly as 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0. The recursion is exhaustive because vertices are ordered along a required Hamilton path, predecessor edges are forced, parity determines all possible extra edges, and forbidden induced subgraphs persist under extensions. Thus a graph in the subclass cannot contain a 15-vertex simple path. In an undirected DFS forest every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints, and root-to-leaf paths have at most 14 vertices. Ancestor bags therefore form a tree decomposition of width at most 13. Standard retained-connectivity partition dynamic programming solves FVS exactly at fixed width.
claims.witness: The exact enumeration count is zero at order 15; the resulting DFS ancestor bags have size at most 14.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive labeled generation with Boolean adjacency masks, followed by a direct verification of the DFS decomposition.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: Within the ambient class of P8-free bipartite graphs, depth-t branching on the four vertices of an uncovered C4 decides whether a C4-transversal of size at most t exists. Iterative deepening first succeeds at t=r and costs O(4^r n^{O(1)}). For the resulting X, G-X satisfies claim 2. Adding X to every width-13 bag gives width at most r+13. A forest DP records the deleted bag subset and connectivity partition of retained vertices; there are 2^{O(r log r)} states, and introduce-edge and join operations reject exactly cycle-forming combinations. Exact finite checking confirmed the transversal search and augmented decomposition on all 512 labeled 3-by-3 bipartite graphs.
claims.witness: A minimum C4-transversal X together with the width-13 decomposition of G-X and its X-augmented bags certifies the parameter bound.
claims.search_method: Direct branching and tree-decomposition proof, supplemented by exhaustive integer-bit-mask validation.

claims.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
claims.evidence: In H_n, neighborhoods are all distinct and nested, so there are no false twins and no induced 2K2, hence no P5. Retaining all B vertices and a_{n-1},a_n proves a C4-transversal of size n-2. Conversely, if i<j are the two smallest retained A-indices, C4-freeness allows at most one retained b_l with l at least j, giving at most n+2 retained vertices and therefore at least n-2 deletions; cases with fewer than two retained A vertices are stronger. For m at least two, the union of m internally disjoint length-three u-v paths has 2m+2 vertices, is bipartite and 2-connected, and every cycle formed by two branches has length six, so it is C4-free. Its hub-layer structure bounds induced paths below eight vertices. Finally, K3,3 has integer FVS optimum two, while assigning exactly 1/4 to every vertex satisfies all induced-C4 constraints with objective 3/2. Exact construction checks and rational arithmetic confirmed these witnesses.
claims.witness: The half graphs H_n, the length-three theta graphs with m branches, and the uniform 1/4 assignment on K3,3.
claims.search_method: General symbolic proofs for both infinite families, bounded exhaustive checks for representative sizes, and exact Fraction arithmetic for K3,3.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an exact polynomial-time algorithm on every P8-free bipartite graph. The draft does not provide one: O(8^k n^8) and the r-parameter algorithm are exponential when their parameters grow with n, the 8-approximation is not exact, and the polynomial exact algorithm applies only to C4-free instances. These are correct and material advances but leave unrestricted C4-containing instances unresolved. The draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is therefore accurate, and its final writeup explicitly disclaims full target resolution rather than overstating coverage.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source JSON and iteration-5 draft; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior frontier run, verification report, or other solution.
Compared the guarantees directly with the exact target and independently classified coverage as valid partial progress.

Independently reproduced the order-1-through-15 enumeration 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 and checked the DFS width implication.
